title: Electrical and Computer Engineering Technology, B.S. (Behrend)
notes: Penn State Erie, The Behrend College -- a genuinely separate major from University Park's Electrical Engineering Technology, B.S. (EET-2026.json), confirmed by direct bulletin comparison 2026-08-27: this is a different degree title entirely ('Electrical and Computer Engineering Technology' vs. UP's plain 'Electrical Engineering Technology'), taught with Behrend's own EET-2/EET-101/EET-109/CMPET-5 first-year sequence that doesn't exist at UP at all, and diverging further from there -- not a 2+2 feeder. Built fresh (Pattern B) as EETBH per this session's new-major-code convention (closest UP code EET + 'BH'). The real Behrend program has two credit-equivalent options (Electrical Engineering Technology option and Computer Engineering Technology option) sharing an identical first two years; this plan models the CMPET (Computer Engineering Technology) option specifically for its third/fourth years, same single-path convention ME-2026 already uses for its own A-K/L-Z split. The EET option was NOT chosen because its own real fourth-year-Fall requirement, EET 416, has a live catalog prereq of EET 315 AND (MATH 211 or MATH 231) AND MATH 250 -- MATH 250 needs MATH 141, and neither MATH 140 nor MATH 141 appear anywhere in this program's real technical-math ladder (MATH 81/83/210/211), which would require fabricating an entire unrelated calculus sequence to close; the CMPET option's parallel courses (CMPET 456/457) have no such gap. Real 8-semester Suggested Academic Plan (CMPET option), 129 total credits, taken verbatim from the live 2026-27 Behrend bulletin page. 'Tech Elective' (x3, Fourth Year) wired via match to the bulletin's own real School-Approved Electives footnote (CMPET option may also take EET 330/416/440; both options may take EET 395/397/461/475/495/496/497). Real-prereq-chain fixes (same 'close the real gap' convention as every other major in this repo): (1) EET 114's real catalog prereq is EET 105 (Electrical Systems) AND MATH 26 -- EET 105 never appears on Behrend's own suggested plan at all (Behrend's plan starts its own EET 101/109 sequence instead, a genuinely different intro course); added EET 105 (Semester 1) since it needs only MATH 21. (2) MATH 22 (a real, already-present Semester-1 course, needed for CHEM 110) itself needs MATH 21, not in the plan; added MATH 21 (Semester 1). (3) EET 101's real catalog concurrent requirement is literally MATH 81 (not MATH 22, which is what this plan's own real Semester-1 math course is) and EGT 119 (Second Year Spring) has a real prereq of MATH 81 too; added MATH 81 (Semester 1, no real prereq of its own) to satisfy both.
